technical_and_design_decisions: All development will target Spring XD's existing modular architecture, leveraging its plugin system for new modules.
For U1, the implementation will follow the suggested approach of handling cleanup in the container during consumer undeployment, using RabbitAdmin.getQueueProperties() to check consumer counts.
For U2, the error channel integration will follow Spring Integration patterns, using a dedicated error channel per stream/module that can be tapped via a standardized interface.
For U3, the initial implementation will use Spring Security's method-level and URL-based security for REST endpoints, with a configuration mechanism using Spring Boot properties.
For U4, the work is purely documentation, capturing all available placeholders from Spring XD's context in the official user guide.
For U5, a new 'http-mvc' module will be created as a separate artifact, embedding Tomcat and configuring Spring MVC/Security in a self-contained manner, distinct from the existing http source.

For U6, the client-side will implement a polling mechanism with backoff, while server-side will leverage Spring's ApplicationEvent mechanism to propagate state changes between admin, containers, and eventually clients.
For U7, the new SFTP source module will be based on Spring Integration's SFTP adapters, with a testing strategy using an embedded SFTP server.
For U8, the new ElasticSearch sink will use Spring Data's ElasticsearchTemplate or the Elasticsearch Java client, configured via a properties file for connection details.
A dedicated, time-boxed 'spike' activity is included for the research and design phase of U3.
assumptions: The developer has existing knowledge of and access to the Spring XD codebase and its build system.
A working development environment with Java 17+, Maven/Gradle, and necessary Spring XD dependencies is already configured.
Access to test instances of RabbitMQ, SFTP servers, and ElasticSearch is available for integration testing, or can be stood up quickly (e.g., using Docker).
The scope for U3 is limited to the backend REST API and DSL shell as described; the Admin UI integration is deferred to a separate, future story.
The 'clean' functionality in U1 is a best-effort, optional operation. It does not guarantee removal if producers are active or other consumers are present.
For U6, the server-side event propagation is an initial foundation; full real-time event streaming to UI clients is a follow-up enhancement.
All module development (U5, U7, U8) includes writing unit tests and integration tests, but performance testing is not in scope.
Documentation updates (U4) will follow existing Spring XD documentation standards and be added to the relevant wiki/asciidoc files.
The effort estimates assume no major interruptions and that code reviews are performed by a peer, with minimal rework expected.
